title: How Ansible Automation Works
objective: Explain the control-node, managed-node, inventory, module, and playbook model.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 01 - Introduction
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Ansible is an agentless automation system. You install Ansible on a control node, describe managed nodes in inventory, and connect to those nodes—normally over SSH—to inspect or converge their state.

A module performs one focused operation, such as managing a package or file. A playbook records an ordered, repeatable set of module calls in YAML so the same intent can be reviewed, versioned, and rerun.

Automation is valuable when it replaces inconsistent manual steps with declared outcomes. A good first question is not “what command do I want to run?” but “what state should every targeted system end in?”
explanation.rule: Keep automation on the control node; managed nodes do not need a permanent Ansible agent.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
architecture:
  control_node: controller
  inventory: inventory.yml
  managed_nodes:
    - web01
    - web02
    - db01
  transport: ssh
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Explain the control-node, managed-node, inventory, module, and playbook model.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

lab.title: Inspect the prepared controller
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Open the Terminal tab and run ansible --version.
Print /workspace/inventory.yml and identify the two inventory groups.
Run ansible all --list-hosts and predict the three host names.
